subject: ggplot: multiple line plots in one frame

messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: ggplot: multiple line plots in one frame
parts:
I hope it's OK to ask about ggplot here; I see ggplot2 is still in beta
so I thought my life would be easier with ggplot.

I have several different categories of data, identified by the variable
"type." I want a plot in which plots of the different types are
superimposed. Each individual plot should have lines connecting its
points. The problem is that the lines insist on connecting points
belonging to different types.

I tried
qplot(x=beta1, y=reject, data=b1, facets = varb~nsamp, type=c("line",
"point"), colour=type, linetype=type)

b1 has sections stacked vertically with the different types, i.e., first
all entries for one type appear, then the next, and so on.

"line" is supposed to go left to right; it does, but it passes through
points of each type along the way.

I also tried "paths" for plot type; this is a bit better, but it draws a
line back from the one of one type (that's my type variable, not the
plot type) to the start of the next.

Is there a way to get what I want, which is the logic of "line" applied
separately to each type?

Thanks.
Ross


ggplot 0.4.1; R 2.7.1 on Debian GNU/Linux. I originally installed
ggplot and related packages June 2007; I've reinstalled ggplot, but not
the others, under my current R.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: ggplot: multiple line plots in one frame
parts:
Hi Ross,

ggplot2 is definitely the package you want to use - ggplot has been
retired now. Is type categorical or continuous? If it's continuous,
you'll also need to specify group = type to have one line for each
value of type.

Hadley

> qplot(x=beta1, y=reject, data=b1, facets = varb~nsamp, geom=c("path", "point"), colour=type, linetype=type)
Error in get("new", env = FacetGrid, inherits = TRUE)(FacetGrid, ...) :
could not find function "is.formula"

I'm not sure if colour or linetype are appropriate for ggplot2, but I
get the same error without them.

http://tolstoy.newcastle.edu.au/R/devel/04/08/0502.html indicates
is.formula disappeared as far back as R 1.9.1

Ross
